To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
telephone counseling was associated with a lower rate of testing, and the association was moderated by race/ethnicity.

1) the uptake of testing was significantly lower in the telephone group than in the face-to-face group; 2) the uptake was higher in women with higher perceived stress and knowledge; 3) the uptake was lower in women of minority races/ethnicities and in the telephone group; and 4) the uptake was significantly lower in women of African-American or Hispanic descent in the telephone group.
the uptake of genetic testing in a randomized trial was lower in the telephone group than in the in-person group.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we found that telephone counseling was not inferior to in-person counseling, and that telephone counseling may be a good alternative to in-person counseling for women who have difficulty getting to in-person sessions.
telephone genetic counseling is effective and efficient, and that it can increase access for women who otherwise would be unable to receive genetic counseling and testing.
telephone-based genetic counseling is an effective way to increase the uptake of BRCA1 and BRCA2 testing among high-risk individuals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
telephone counseling can be a useful alternative to in-person counseling.

telephone-based genetic counseling can be a very effective method for delivering this service to women who are interested in learning more about their personal risk of hereditary cancer, but it is important that the service provider be aware of and sensitive to the potential barriers that may prevent some women, particularly minority women, from taking advantage of this option.
telephone genetic counseling is a viable and cost-effective way to increase access to genetic testing.
